title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: An Artifact-backed Null and Reproducibility Report
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to test whether a composite canary–rollback score (verifier coverage, canary-sim pass, rollback-success probability, LLM confidence, abstention utility) discriminates emulator-measured outages better than the best single submetric. Using a deterministic synthetic NetOps task bank, a deterministic validator, and the declared LLM (gpt-5-mini), we ran 200 held-out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded). All 200 test pairs succeeded in both conditions (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0); paired-difference = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]; McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The preregistered AUC-ROC primary estimand could not be computed because test labels are constant. We document the exact persisted artifacts (paths and SHA-256s) that support these facts, report one artifact-collection omission that prevents recomputing the preregistered AUC comparison (missing: consolidated per-episode submetric CSV and serialized trained-composite-model weights), and provide a deterministic reconstruction recipe and operational recommendations for future discriminative NetOps evaluations.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLM workflows promise fast intent→configuration translation for NetOps but raise critical assurance questions: when may a proposed change increase outage risk? Standard operational safeguards include deterministic validators, canary simulations, rollback trials, and abstention policies. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to test a practical, operational question: does a composite score that combines verifier coverage, canary-sim pass, rollback-success probability, model confidence, and an abstention-utility proxy discriminate emulator-measured outage risk better than any single submetric on held-out synthetic NetOps tasks? The study design (train/val/test splits, estimands, analysis) and artifact-capture requirements were frozen before execution (preregistration SHA-256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee). Our run produced a deterministic, fully hashed evidence bundle. The principal scientific outcome is an artifact-traced null/ceiling result (no observed outages on test) and a reproducibility diagnosis that identifies a missing persisted artifact required to compute the preregistered AUC comparison.
sections.related_work: Prior work frames verifier-interposition and generate–verify–repair architectures as essential for operational correctness of LLM-generated outputs [1,2,3]. Sequential verifier-orchestration and cost-aware verification policies motivate canary and rollback instrumentation to trade verification cost and operational risk [4]. Our contribution is experimental and reproducibility-oriented: a fully preregistered paired execution with preserved validator traces and model-provider call logs that documents a ceiling outcome and identifies concrete artifact-hygiene deficits that block recomputation of the preregistered discriminative estimand. Representative prior sources used for positioning are cited and verified in the evidence bundle (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental plan. The preregistration (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1; SHA-256 cited above) fixed: model family (declared gpt-5-mini; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), synthetic task bank generation and deterministic splits (train=300,val=100,test=200), paired baseline vs guarded condition, primary estimand (difference in AUC-ROC: composite vs best single submetric), analysis recipe (L2 logistic regression with 5-fold CV on train+val, DeLong for AUC difference, paired bootstrap for CI with seed=1729 and 10000 resamples), stopping and missingness rules, and required persisted artifacts (per-episode scoring JSONs, consolidated per-episode submetric CSV, serialized trained-composite-model weights). The preregistration hash is recorded in the execution manifest (see Disclosure). Execution and persistent artifacts. The run used a deterministic shared-initial generation policy per task. For each episode we persisted raw model outputs (execution/responses/*.txt), deterministic per-episode scoring JSONs with validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), and an execution manifest (paths and full hash manifest included in the bundle). Representative persisted artifacts and authoritative hashes: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951. Scoring and submetrics (preregistered). The preregistration defined five submetrics per episode: (a) verifier_coverage (fraction of required parsed/validated commands observed by the validator); (b) canary_sim_pass (deterministic canary simulation pass flag aggregated across canonical seeds); (c) rollback_success_prob (scripted rollback trial success probability in emulator); (d) LLM_confidence (model-provided confidence or proxy); (e) abstention_utility (simple utility proxy quantifying benefit of abstaining). The preregistration required persisting a consolidated per-episode submetric CSV and serialized trained-composite-model weights; those two artifacts are not present in the evidence bundle (see Results), which prevents recomputing the preregistered AUC-ROC composite comparison from persisted artifacts alone.
sections.results: Authoritative artifact-backed facts (exact persisted counts and hashes). The execution manifest (bundle) records planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the bundle). The persisted per-episode scoring JSONs yield the binary outcome label validator_trace.validation_after.valid for every test episode. On the held-out test partition (N=200 pairs) the persisted scoring JSONs show baseline_success_count = 200/200 and guarded_success_count = 200/200. The paired contingency table persisted at analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) records: n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. The pre-registered paired hypothesis (McNemar exact two-sided) yields p = 1.0 (test applied to persisted contingency counts). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000 as preregistered) is [0.0,0.0]. Primary AUC estimand: uncomputable from supplied artifacts. Because the held-out outcome vector is constant (no positive outage labels among the 200 test examples) the preregistered AUC-ROC comparison (composite vs best single submetric) is undefined and therefore cannot be evaluated from the supplied bundle. Missing persisted artifacts that block recomputation. The preregistration required persisting (1) a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV and (2) the serialized trained-composite-model weights. These two artifacts are absent from the evidence bundle. The persisted artifacts that are present and authoritative (enough to reconstruct certain steps) include execution/scoring/*.json (validator traces with normalization and parsed counts), execution/provider_calls/*.json, execution/responses/*.txt, and the analysis CSVs noted above. Representative persisted examples and their SHA-256s are cited above and are included in the bundle. Per-preregistered-submetric availability (artifact-grounded). Using the persisted scoring JSON schema (execution/scoring/*.json) and provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json) we determine availability for each preregistered submetric: - verifier_coverage: present — computable from execution/scoring/<episode>.json fields validator_trace.validation_after.observed_touched_field_count and validator_trace.validation_after.required_command_count (example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2b...). - canary_sim_pass: absent from persisted artifacts — no canary_sim_result key present in execution/provider_calls/*.json nor in execution/scoring/*.json in the supplied bundle; the preregistration required deriving this by running a deterministic canary simulator or by persisting the value, but the value was not persisted. - rollback_success_prob: absent — no explicit rollback_trial_result or rollback_success field appears in the persisted provider-call trace entries in the supplied bundle. - LLM_confidence: absent — execution/responses/*.txt and provider_call traces in the bundle do not include a numeric model-confidence field for episodes (no canonical key present). - abstention_utility: absent — no persisted abstain_decision or abstention-utility field in execution/provider_calls or scoring JSONs. Reproduction recipe (artifact-only reconstruction limits). Deterministic reconstruction steps that can be performed from persisted artifacts: (i) extract per-episode binary labels from execution/scoring/*.json at validator_trace.validation_after.valid; (ii) compute verifier_coverage per episode as observed_touched_field_count / required_command_count; (iii) re-create the paired contingency table and McNemar test exactly (these files are already persisted: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 7bc1...); (iv) if and only if the missing per-episode submetrics (canary, rollback, confidence, abstention) are present in execution/provider_calls/*.json (they are not in this bundle) one can assemble the full per-episode feature matrix and retrain the composite model using the preregistered L2 logistic regression with 5-fold CV. Because the consolidated submetric CSV and trained weights were not persisted, step (iv) requires re-running the canary/rollback simulations or regenerating the missing submetrics, which would create derived artifacts and therefore depart from the preserved artifact set; we do not fabricate them here. Representative scoring JSON excerpt (artifact-backed example). execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA-256 = 90844c2b...) contains validator_trace.validation_after with parsed_command_count=4, required_command_count=4, observed_touched_field_count=3, normalized_configuration and final_state; these fields enable verifier_coverage computation and authoritative valid/invalid labeling used in the paired analysis.
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded interpretation and practical lessons. The observed ceiling (no outage positives in test) can be explained without inventing new data: the synthetic task bank and deterministic validator used in this run produced candidate configurations that satisfied the validator predicates across both conditions. Consequences for discriminative evaluation: (1) when test labels are constant a discriminative AUC-based estimand is undefined; (2) to evaluate residual-risk metrics one must design test partitions with seeded adverse cases or controlled nondeterminism so positive labels appear at nontrivial prevalence; (3) artifact hygiene matters: always persist consolidated per-episode submetric summaries and serialized trained-model weights so preregistered discriminative comparisons are reproducible and auditable. Reproducibility diagnosis and required-fixes (concrete, artifact-grounded). The bundle contains exhaustive per-episode scoring JSONs (path execution/scoring/*.json) and provider-call traces (path execution/provider_calls/*.json) plus the analysis CSVs cited above, so third parties can deterministically verify the paired contingency claim and validator traces. The missing persisted artifacts that prevent recomputing the preregistered AUC comparison are: - consolidated per-episode submetric CSV (preregistered file name: consolidated_submetrics.csv — NOT present in execution/), - serialized trained-composite-model weights (preregistered file name: composite_model_weights.pkl — NOT present). We recommend, and recorded in the Disclosure, that future runs persist these exact filenames and a deterministic retrain script (hash) so reproduction is immediate. Threats to validity. Internal: paired design is deterministic and reproducible but subject to design choices in validator semantics and task generation. Construct: emulator/validator correctness vs production outage mapping is limited. External: single model (gpt-5-mini declared), synthetic tasks, and deterministic validator limit generalization. Conclusion validity: sample size N=200 is adequate for paired tests but uninformative when labels are constant. Operational implication: a negative empirical outcome (no observed outages) is informative for the specific synthetic/emulator environment but not evidence that composite risk scoring lacks utility in broader, realistic NetOps settings; instead, it highlights that richer test partitions (seeded faults, adversarial cases) are required to exercise verification/rollback discriminators.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired NetOps experiment that produced an artifact-backed ceiling/null result: every held-out task was validated as correct in both baseline and guarded conditions (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0). The preregistered AUC-based primary estimand was uncomputable from persisted artifacts because test labels are constant; furthermore, two preregistered artifacts required to compute the composite-vs-submetric AUC (consolidated per-episode submetric CSV and serialized trained-composite-model weights) were not persisted and are therefore absent from the evidence bundle. The preserved artifacts (responses, per-episode scoring JSONs with validator traces, provider-call traces, execution manifest, analysis CSVs) suffice to verify the reported paired contingency and validator-derived outcomes. The manuscript's main scientific contribution is methodological: it documents a deterministic null outcome, provides an artifact-grounded reproducibility recipe and a precise list of missing persisted artifacts, and issues concrete recommendations (seeded adverse cases, persisted consolidated submetric CSV, persisted trained weights, and a deterministic retrain script) for future discriminative NetOps evaluations that aim to validate composite risk scores in agentic workflows. All cited artifact paths and representative SHA-256 hashes are included below for authoritative verification.

disclosure_statement: Autonomy, pre-lock human role, and immutable initial master prompt. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary prior to the autonomy lock. After the lock, all literature review, preregistration, experiment-design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting reported here were performed autonomously without manual human editing of technical content. Declared LLM and configuration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Immutable initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Preregistration. The preregistered study id is CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1; the preregistration JSON SHA-256 is 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee (recorded in the execution manifest). Evidence retention and omission. The evidence bundle contains per-episode raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json — representative example execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json), and analysis CSVs (analysis/*.csv) with recorded SHA-256 hashes (representative hashes cited in the manuscript). The preregistered artifacts that were NOT persisted into the evidence bundle are (a) the consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV and (b) the serialized trained-composite-model weights file. Because those two artifacts were not persisted, the preregistered AUC-ROC composite-vs-best-submetric comparison cannot be recomputed from the supplied bundle without deterministic reconstruction or re-running canary/rollback simulations (which would create new derived artifacts). Safety and operational scope. Experiments used synthetic tasks and containerized emulators only; no production devices or proprietary vendor images were used. No technical restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0). All retained artifacts are hashed and listed in the execution manifest; representative hashes are cited above and in the manuscript.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real-world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single-model execution: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator-derived outage labels may not map one-to-one to production outage risk in real networks.

Artifact omission: serialized trained-composite-model weights and a consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV were not persisted to the evidence bundle (documented execution artifact-collection omission).
